that the message of a crown is that we are leaders. True, we Yidden are often not the biggest group

in our city. There are usually only a few of us compared to everyone else. And there are even fewer of us chayolim! But we must always remember that no matter what, we are leaders, not followers. When we march in the streets on Lag BaOmer, we remember that this is the day of the great leader, Rabi Shimon bar Yochai. He was one of the first tanna’im, and his teachings continue to be learned until today!

Therefore, we wear special crowns, shout the pesukim really loudly, and remember that each of us are leaders, too!

We have a special minhag to eat carobs (called “ּבאָקְסעֶר” in Yiddish) on Lag BaOmer. This is because Lag BaOmer is when Rabi Shimon bar Yochai (“Rashbi”) passed away. When he and his son were hiding in a cave for thirteen years, they survived by eating carobs that miraculously grew outside the cave. To remember the neis, we eat carobs, too. Be sure to check for bugs before eating, and careful not to crack your teeth!

On Lag BaOmer, the Rebbe encouraged everyone to give tzedaka in multiples of 18. (Can you name three such multiples?) Lag BaOmer falls on Chai (Yud-Ches) Iyar—the gematria of 18. This day gives chayus to the whole month’s avoda, so it’s a good day to give tzedaka in amounts connected to 18.

Let’s back up. The reason why we do mourn during Sefira is because most of Rabi Akiva’s talmidim passed away. They didn’t have proper Ahavas Yisroel. But on Lag BaOmer, they stopped dying! The Rebbe told us children that it’s our job throughout the month of Iyar—and specifically on Lag BaOmer—to behave with extra Ahavas Yisroel. This will help bring Moshiach much faster, and then we’ll never need to mourn during Sefira

Further Reading: Likkutei Sichos, vol. 32, pp. 254–256;

Toras Menachem, vol. 3, pp. 77–81; Der Rebbe Redt Tzu Kinder, vol. 3, pp.

157–160, 231–234; Sichos Kodesh 5740, vol. 3, pp. 201–202.

Do you know which sefer Rabi Shimon bar Yochai wrote?

He wrote the Zohar Hakadosh, a very special sefer about Pnimiyus HaTorah. Rashbi was one of the first people to write down such deep Torah secrets, and on the day that he passed away, there was a tremendous giluy of these secrets for all of Klal Yisroel. And guess what? Rashbi says that the same thing will happen for the generation that ends Golus and greets Moshiach—both adults and children alike will learn the deepest secrets of the Torah, and through this bring the Geulah!

Lag BaOmer is a happy day. It is a day to sing, dance, and rejoice with extra simcha! Here’s a story about how important it is to be happy on this day:

A certain talmid of the Arizal felt so broken about the Churban Beis Hamikdash that he would say “נַחֵם” (a tefilla we say on Tisha B’Av) every day of the year. One Lag BaOmer, he came with the Arizal to Meiron, where Rashbi is buried. That day, he said “nacheim” as usual.

Rashbi soon appeared to the Arizal with a message. He told him that on such a happy day like Lag BaOmer, his talmid should not say “nacheim”. For doing so, he would be punished.

We can all take a lesson from this to be happy on Lag BaOmer. Even someone who truly mourned the Beis Hamikdash was not allowed to do so on Lag BaOmer. Let’s be sure to fill ourselves with simcha this Lag BaOmer! Gut Yom Tov!

Lag BaOmer has a specific toy connected to it: the bow and arrow! “Bow” in Hebrew is a קֶשֶׁת, which is also the word for rainbow. Rainbows are Hashem’s reminder that He won’t destroy the world with another Mabul. But as long as Rashbi was alive, not a single rainbow was needed; his z’chus protected the world! To remember this, we play with bows and arrows.

The Rebbe also teaches us a deep lesson from how a bow is used: When you pull the arrow towards yourself, it can fly forward. Only when it’s pulled back really far—all the way to your heart—will the arrow fly powerfully.

The same is with Avodas Hashem. In order to serve Hashem properly, we need to “pull the string” of bittul close to our heart. This means that by learning Torah with humility (and not because “I am so great and smart”), our “arrow” can fly powerfully against the Yetzer Hara!

Are you ready to practice your aim this Lag BaOmer?

Parades are a great way to show that we are proud to be Yidden! The Rebbe arranged children’s parades in front of 770 even before he became Rebbe! תשט”ז )1956( was the first Lag BaOmer “marching parade”. Originally, the parades didn’t happen every year. They would only be arranged when Lag BaOmer fell out on a Sunday, so public school children could attend. The Rebbe spoke at many of them; the last such parade was in תש”נ)1990(. But in תש”מ )1980(, the Rebbe instructed that we should make a parade every Lag BaOmer in neighborhoods and cities all over. This way, we show the world how proud we are to be chayolim, following in the ways of Pnimiyus HaTorah that Rashbi gave us. At the parades, we make sure to say the twelve pesukim loudly and proudly, and march with smiles on our faces and our heads held high!
